chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Jumhoor narrated together, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jumhoor, from his father, from Sulayman ibn Sama'ah, from Abul Jarood, from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid al-Hamdani, from al-Harith al-A'war al-Hamdani, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Blessed is the son of the best of the bondmaids (he means the Qa'im from his progeny). He will humiliate them, and water them with a bitter nauseous drink, and give them nothing but the sword causing slaughter. At that time, the scoundrels of Quraysh will wish that they could ransom themselves with the world and all that is in it to be forgiven. He will not cease from them until Allah is pleased.'

key_terms.ابْنُ خَيْرَةِ الْأِمَّاءِ: Son of the best of the bondmaids, a title for the Mahdi referring to his mother, Fatimah al-Awsat
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Awakened One, referring to the Twelfth Imam, Muhammad al-Mahdi

ai.seo_question: What are the deeds and characteristics of the Qa'im according to this hadith from Kitab al-Ghayba?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this hadith from the chain of al-Jarudi emphasizes the eschatological justice of the Qa'im, who will subdue the arrogant through both spiritual and physical means. The imagery of the 'bitter drink' and the 'sword' reflects the dual nature of his rule, culminating in the repentance of the Quraysh elite who will desire a ransom to escape divine retribution. This narrative underscores the Shia belief in the ultimate purification of the earth from tyranny, aligning with the concept of *Adl* (divine justice).
